answer: Treat the economy as a graph: each identity is a vertex, each verified trade a weighted edge. Trust is eigenvector centrality, so a vertex gains standing only through trades with already-trusted vertices, and a Sybil cluster trading among itself stays near zero however many fakes it spawns. Like a willow, trust grows slowly from established roots: to climb, an identity posts a 50-unit anchor bond and completes 20 verified trades with high-centrality partners. One fraud report zeroes the vertex and forfeits the bond, so 100 fakes cost 5,000 units and still gain nothing.
